title: What first round vote share will Iliana Iotova win in the 2026 Bulgarian Presidential election?
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the percentage vote share received by Iliana Iotova in the first round of the Bulgarian presidential election scheduled to be held on October 25, 2026, as declared by the [Bulgarian Central Election Commission](https://results.cik.bg/).
fine_print: If the election is postponed or cancelled such that no result is declared on or before December 31, 2026, this question will be **annulled**.

comments.author: Vlad25
comments.text: I've made my prediction based on the average of five recent polls which all put Lotova's support at approximately 46.9%. I do think that turnout and differences in polling methods could affect the final result, I still believe this is still a reasonable estimate.

comments.author: VectorWright
comments.text:
Good thread. The historical/structural analyses here (tejvn's outlier-adjusted base rate, Theomachado's coalition-backing method comparing to Progressive Bulgaria's 44.6% April 2026 parliamentary result) both land in the low-to-mid 40s. But the actual Oct 5 polls Theomachado flagged, Alpha Research 44.5% and Myara 46.9%, plus MaxA's second linked poll at 50.2% among decided voters, pull the real-time picture a bit higher than the structural models alone.



DeRuina's point is worth holding onto though. Raw vote-count projections only read as a near-majority if turnout collapses, and the CEC denominator may include an "I support nobody" line that trims every candidate's share by about a point. That's a real source of downward pressure the headline poll numbers don't account for.



I'm landing at a median of 47, with a 44 to 50 interquartile range. Close to Theomachado's updated 46% but shaded a touch higher given the more recent polling, especially that 50.2% decided-voter number. Keeping the tails modest too: 1% below 35, 3% above 55, since the field isn't even finalized yet and there's still real room for a late entrant or an undecided-voter surprise.

comments.author: Theomachado
comments.text:
# POLLS UPDATE - OCT 5th

comments.author: DeRuina
comments.text: One thing I'd flag: Andrey Raychev's projection (quoted around 23–24 September, novini247) of roughly 1.1 million votes for Iotova only becomes a near-majority share if turnout collapses. Radev's 49.4% in 2021 came from about 1.32 million votes on 40.5% turnout, roughly 2.7 million ballots cast. Market Links' Zhivkov expects turnout below 50% this time, but even 45% means around 3 million ballots, and 1.1 million of those lands in the high 30s, not near Radev's result. So the sociologists' raw vote estimates and the share expectations floating around here may not be describing the same election. Worth checking too whether the CEC denominator includes the "I support nobody" line, which trims every candidate's share by a point or so.

comments.author: Theomachado
comments.text:
On 19 April 2026, Radev's Progressive Bulgaria secured 44.6% of the vote and 131 out of 240 seats, achieving a single-party majority with approximately 50% turnout. GERB–SDS fell to 13.4%, PP–DB remained at 12.6%, DPS had its lowest result since 1994, and BSP did not enter parliament for the first time in modern Bulgarian history.

Iotova is the bloc's candidate, with the election scheduled six months after the parliamentary vote. This result provides the most recent and reliable measure of her coalition's support, offering stronger evidence than any current poll.

**The reference class compares** each first-round share to the combined vote of the parties supporting that candidate in the most recent parliamentary election.

| 2006 | Parvanov   | 64.05% | BSP + NDSV + DPS \= 63.64%        | +0.41 |
| ---- | ---------- | ------ | --------------------------------- | ----- |
| 2011 | Plevneliev | 40.11% | GERB \= 39.72%                    | +0.39 |
| 2021 | Radev      | 49.42% | PP + BSPzB + ITN + IBG-NI ≈ 46.1% | +3.3  |

Two important caveats apply.

The 2021 delta is sensitive to how coalitions are defined. Including Democratic Bulgaria (6.37%) among Radev's supporters changes the result to −3.0. This figure should be considered ambiguous rather than definitive.

Large positive deltas cited from earlier cycles (Zhelev 1992, Radev 2016) occur only when comparing to a single party rather than the entire supporting bloc. Accurately defining the coalition is essential for meaningful analysis.

Therefore, I estimate support in the mid-40s, with a narrower spread than the 25.4–64.0 range observed across seven previous elections. This historical range is mainly due to variations in coalition size.

***

**Data used and analysed**

* **CIK declared results** (results.cik.bg) 
* **Parliamentary results for each backing coalition** 
* **April 2026 parliamentary result**, 
* **Global Metrics conducted fieldwork from 23 June to 11 July 2026** 
* **Macro context** (Eurostat: HICP, unemployment, consumer confidence through August 2026)
